and those who wear matted hair and bark garments outside of the forest-dweller's stage of life, / being engaged in non-Vedic practices—they indeed are heretics.
Those twice-born who are devoid of the conch, discus, vertical sectarian mark, and other signs / most dear to Hari, O goddess—they indeed are considered heretics.
That twice-born who does not practice the conduct taught in the Śruti and Smṛti / is to be known as a heretic, condemned in all the worlds.
Those [who act] without devotion to the Blessed Lord are indeed considered heretics. / When one offers in sacrifice or gives gifts by designating other deities alone,
[ignoring] Viṣṇu who is the enjoyer of all sacrifices, the supreme deity of the sacred lore— / he is to be known as a heretic, acting independently in all rituals.
He who performs an important rite enjoined in the Veda independently, / or who looks upon the god Nārāyaṇa as equal
to other deities such as Brahmā and Rudra—he is ever a heretic. / A twice-born who does not know Vāsudeva in all three states
with mind, speech, body, and actions, is a heretic. / What is the use of saying much here? Even if they are brāhmaṇas, those who are not Vaiṣṇavas
should never be touched, spoken to, or looked upon. / Pārvatī said: / O Lord, best of deities, I ask a supreme secret.
Explain it to me out of love; a great doubt exists [in me]. / The wearing of a skull, ashes, hide, and bones is condemned by the Śruti;
why is that condemned [practice] borne by you, O god? / Out of a woman's curiosity, O Lord of gods, I ask you, O noble-minded one.
Because of great majesty it was said that it should never be done by anyone; / this was not explained by you in detail formerly, O great Lord.
You ought to forgive this question of mine about what should not be done, O Lord. / Vasiṣṭha said: / Thus questioned by the goddess in a secret place deserted by people,
Hara spoke the supreme secret concerning whatever practices he had performed. / Śiva said: / Listen, O goddess, I shall declare that secret which is exceedingly wonderful.
It should not be spoken among people, O goddess, when told by me. / Because of the non-difference of your body [from mine], I will tell it to you, O faithful one.
Formerly, in the Svāyambhuva interval, the great daityas headed by Namuci— / possessed of great strength, great heroism, great courage, and great splendour,
all devoted to Viṣṇu, pure, devoid of all sins, / and adhering to the religion of the three Vedas—defeated [the gods] headed by Indra.
Having come near Viṣṇu, afflicted with fear, they took refuge. / The gods said: / [They are] unconquerable by all the gods, their sins cleansed by asceticism;
you alone, O Keśava, are able to conquer these great daityas. / Mahādeva said: / Hearing this dreadful speech of the gods, Hari,
having comforted those guardians of the directions, the Supreme Person spoke to me. / The Blessed Lord said: / O Rudra, O mighty-armed one, for the sake of deluding the enemies of the gods,
adopt a dharma characterized by the practice of heresy, O best of gods, / and proclaim to them Purāṇas full of darkness (tamas);
and compose delusive treatises, O noble-minded one. / Thus those brāhmaṇas and great sages will become estranged from me.
Possessing them with devotion to me, tell them the tāmasa [teachings]: / Kaṇāda, Gautama, Śakti, Upamanyu, and Jaimini,
and also Kapila, Durvāsas, Mṛkaṇḍu, Bṛhaspati, / and Bhārgava Jāmadagnya—these ten tāmasa sages.
Possessing them with your power of disposition, do what brings about good for the world; / and entered by your power, in which darkness is exceedingly dominant,
they will become tāmasa in an instant, without a doubt; / those brahmins will narrate the tāmasa [doctrines] throughout the three worlds.
Purāṇas and scriptures [will be] reinforced by you with reality, / [along with] signs of skulls, hides, ashes, and bones entirely, O immortal one.
You yourself have borne them; delude the worlds in the three worlds. / Likewise, you yourself, highly honored, compose the Pāśupata scripture,
through the divisions of the Kaṅkāla, Śaiva, heretical, Mahāśaiva, and others. / The vile men [will uphold] an unmanifest doctrine completely outside the Veda.
All bearing ashes and bones will indeed become devoid of sense; / tāmasa men will proclaim you as the supreme in all scriptures.
Relying upon their doctrine, all the primeval Daityas / will turn away from me in an instant, without a doubt.
Even I, in my incarnations, worship you, O mighty Rudra, / from age to age, for the purpose of deluding the tāmasa ones.

Taking hold of this doctrine, they certainly fall, without a doubt.
Mahādeva said: / Hearing what was spoken by Vāsudeva in this way, O lady,
I became utterly wretched in countenance at this, O fair-faced one. / Then, having bowed down to that god, the supreme lord, I said:
If, O Lord, I carry out on the surface of the earth what has been spoken by you, / from that will come my destruction, O Master; there is no doubt.
How can this deed be done by me now, O Hari? / And your command cannot be transgressed; this is a very great sorrow.
When this was said, O goddess, comforting me once again, / Hari said to me: “Let this not be for your self-destruction here.
For the benefit of the gods, carry out my word; / I shall also tell you the means of your sustenance, O best of gods.
Out of grace he gave me a thousand names of himself: / “Fixing me in your heart, mutter my imperishable mantra.
The six-syllable great mantra is called the liberating Brahman; / for those who mutter it with devotion to me, liberation is beyond doubt.
Dark as a blue-lotus petal, with eyes like lotus leaves, / holding a conch, limbs, bow, and arrows, adorned with all ornaments,
clad in yellow garments, four-armed, beloved of Jānakī— / thus the supreme mantra is to be uttered: ‘Obeisance to Śrī Rāma.’
This removes all sorrow and gives liberation even to sinners; / constantly muttering this mantra, you will become taintless.
The sin that arose in you from bearing ashes, bones, and the like / has all become auspicious through the pure utterance of my mantra.
Gratified, I shall destroy every sin, O best of gods; / devotion to another deity than me does not arise, O one of good vows.
Worship me with the mind alone in your heart, the master, the supreme Person; / fulfill my command for love of me; all this is auspicious for you.”
Having thus instructed me, O goddess, he dismissed the hosts of Maruts; / having been dismissed, the gods then returned and went to their own hermitage.

Then the gods, led by Indra, implored me.
Indra and the others said: / Quickly accomplish what is beneficial, O god, as Hari has just spoken.
Mahādeva said: / For the sake of the gods' welfare, O auspicious one, the way of the heretics— / bearing the skull, hide, ashes, and bones—was adopted by me.
The tāmasa Purāṇas, as spoken by Viṣṇu, O auspicious one, / and the heretical Śaiva scriptures, I composed as instructed.
Entering the brahmins, Gautama and the rest, with my power, / scriptures outside the Veda were fully proclaimed by me, O sinless one.
Relying on this doctrine, all the wicked Rākṣasas, / turned away from the Blessed One, were all enveloped by darkness.
Bearing ashes and the like, occupied with terrible austerities, / they worshipped me alone with flesh, blood, sandalwood, and other things.
Having obtained boons granted by me, haughty through the power of intoxicated pride, / exceedingly attached to sensory objects, full of lust and anger,
devoid of goodness and lacking vigor, they were then conquered by the hosts of gods; / fallen from all dharma, in time they go to a vile destination.
Those who, relying upon my doctrine, wander on the surface of the earth, / destitute of all dharmas, always look upon hell.
Thus, for the benefit of the gods, this conduct, reviled [by the wise], was adopted by me, O goddess; / keeping Viṣṇu's command before me, the bearing of ashes and bones was performed.
This external mark, O goddess, was for the purpose of deluding the enemies; / but constantly meditating internally upon the god Janārdana in my heart,
muttering his mantra designating the liberating Brahman, / which is equal to the thousand names of Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa,

the six-syllable great mantra that causes the lineage of the Raghus to prosper— / constantly muttering it, O goddess, bathed in the nectar of perpetual bliss, / I always enjoy the ultimate bliss of Brahman, O auspicious one.
All this, which was asked by you, has been declared to you, O fair-faced one; / what else do you wish to hear? Inquire of that to me with affection.

6.236.m: Pārvatī said: / Explain to me the tāmasa scriptures, O sinless one, / that were proclaimed by those brahmins devoid of devotion to the Blessed One; / state their names in order, O lord of the gods.
Rudra said: / Listen, O goddess, I shall declare the tāmasa [scriptures] in due order,
by whose mere recollection delusion would come upon even wise men. / First of all, indeed, the Śaiva, Pāśupata, and the like were spoken by me alone.
Hear now those spoken by brahmins possessed by my power: / by Kaṇāda was proclaimed the great Vaiśeṣika scripture;
by Gautama likewise Nyāya; Sāṃkhya indeed by Kapila; / by Dhiṣaṇa was proclaimed the utterly despised Cārvāka doctrine;
for the destruction of the Daityas, by Viṣṇu having assumed the form of Buddha, / the false Buddhist scripture was spoken, along with the naked [Jainas] and blue-robed [sectarians].
Māyāvāda, an untrue scripture, is called disguised Buddhism; / it was uttered by me alone, O goddess, in the Kali age, having assumed the form of a brahmin,
showing a distorted meaning of Vedic texts, reviled by the world; / in this very system, it is established that one's own prescribed actions are to be renounced,
which is called unrighteousness by those fallen from all duties; / moreover, the identity of the individual soul and the supreme Lord is asserted by me,
and the nature of this Brahman will be described by me as devoid of qualities, / for the delusion of the whole world here in the Kali age.
A great scripture having the appearance of Vedic meaning, which through illusion is non-Vedic, / was devised by me alone, O goddess, for the sake of destroying the worlds.
By my command Jaimini previously made the Veda meaningless, / creating an even greater scripture by means of a godless doctrine.
Know these to be the tāmasa scriptures, O daughter of the mountain; / and I shall declare the tāmasa Purāṇas in due order.
The Brāhma, the Pādma, the Vaiṣṇava, the Śaiva, and likewise the Bhāgavata, / as well as the Nāradīya, and the Mārkaṇḍeya as the seventh;
The Āgneya is declared the eighth, and the Bhaviṣya the ninth; / the tenth is the Brahmavaivarta, and the Liṅga is remembered as the eleventh;
The Varāha is the twelfth, the Vāmana the thirteenth, / the Kaurma is declared the fourteenth, and the Mātsya is remembered as the fifteenth;
The Gāruḍa is declared the sixteenth, the Skānda is remembered as the seventeenth, / and the Brahmāṇḍa the eighteenth: [these are] the Purāṇas in order.
The Mātsya, the Kaurma, likewise the Laiṅga, the Śaiva, and similarly the Skānda / and the Āgneya—know from me that these six are tāmasa.
The Vaiṣṇava, the Nāradīya, and the auspicious Bhāgavata, / and the Gāruḍa, the Pādma, and the Vārāha, O woman of fair appearance,
are to be recognized as sattvic Purāṇas, truly auspicious. / The Brahmāṇḍa, the Brahmavaivarta, and likewise the Mārkaṇḍeya,
the Bhaviṣya, the Vāmana, and the Brāhma—know [them] from me as rājasa. / The sattvic are declared givers of liberation; the rājasa always give heaven;
Likewise, O goddess, the tāmasa are causes of entering hell. / In the same way, the Smṛtis were pronounced by the sages as endowed with the three guṇas,
sattvic, rājasa, and tāmasa, O woman of fair appearance. / The Vāsiṣṭha, the Hārīta, the Vyāsa, likewise the Pārāśara,
and the Bhāradvāja and the Kāśyapa are sattvic, auspicious, granting liberation. / The Yājñavalkya, likewise the Ātreya, the Taittira, and also the Dākṣa,
the Kātyāyana, and the Vaiṣṇava are rājasa, giving heaven, auspicious. / The Gautama, the Bārhaspatya, the Sāṃvarta, and what is remembered as the Yama,
the Sāṅkhya, and the Auśanasa—these are tāmasa, granting hell. / What need is there of saying much in this matter regarding the Purāṇas and the Smṛtis?

The tāmasa lead only to hell; a discerning person should avoid them. / All this has been related to you by way of context, O woman of fair appearance; / and I shall declare to you the state of Hari's forms that remain: hear!

6.237.m: The venerable Rudra said: / Hiraṇyaka and Hiraṇyākṣa, the two sons of Kaśyapa, endowed with great strength, / the sons of Diti, of great valor, both lords of all Daityas,
who were named Jaya and Vijaya, went to Hari in Śvetadvīpa. / When Sanaka and the other lords of yoga entered there, those two of great strength
stopped them, O goddess, who were eager to see Hari. / Accursed by them, the two doorkeepers, foremost of gods, of great valor—
Sanaka and the others said: / Leaving that [place], go to the earth, you two servants of the god! / Rudra said: / Having thus given a curse to the two, the lords of sages remained there.
Knowing that matter, the god summoned them and also those two.
Rising there, the Blessed Lord, the cause of the welfare of beings, said to the two: / The Blessed Lord said: / You two of great valor have committed an offense against the great-souled ones.
"This is not to be transgressed by you, O two gatekeepers. / You two sinless ones, who are my devotees, shall endure servitude for seven births."
or three births through enmity, even though worshiping [me]. / Rudra said: / Having been spoken to thus, those two of great valor said to the Supreme Lord:
Jaya and Vijaya said: / We are not able to go to the earth for a long time, O bestower of honor; / therefore, know that we choose births for enmity.
Slain by you yourself, O god, we shall attain your presence! / Rudra said: / Having spoken thus, the two doorkeepers were previously born with great strength,
of Kaśyapa, of great valor, in the womb of Diti, as two great Asuras: / Hiraṇyakaśipu was the elder, Hiraṇyākṣa the younger.
Both were renowned in the worlds, arrogant with great valor and strength. / That extremely haughty Hiraṇyākṣa, whose body was beyond measure,
having uprooted with his thousands of arms the earth along with the mountains, / along with the oceans, endowed with islands, accompanied by all living beings,
having uprooted it and placed it on his head, entered Rasātala. / Then all the hosts of gods cried out, afflicted with fear.
They went for refuge to the imperishable god Nārāyaṇa. / Thereupon, having recognized that extraordinary deed, the wielder of the conch, discus, and mace,
assuming the form of a boar, the all-formed Janārdana, / whose body is without beginning, middle, or end, the omnipresent lord consisting of all the gods,
whose hands, feet, and eyes are everywhere, who has a great tusk and great arms— / with a single tusk, the Supreme Lord slew that Daitya.
His massive limbs crushed, that lowest of the sons of Diti died. / Seeing the earth fallen, having lifted it up with his tusk as before

and established it, he placed it on Śeṣa, [while holding] the body of a tortoise at that time. / Seeing that great Hari in the form of a boar, all the deities / and sages, their bodies bowed in devotion, praised [him]:
The gods said: / Homage to the sacrificial Boar, homage to you who have a hundred arms! / Homage to you, god of gods, homage to you whose form is the universe!
Homage to the nature of preservation, to the one whose nature is all sacrifices, / to the measure of art, the measure of wood, the blinking of an eye; homage to you whose form is time!
Homage to you, the self of living beings, and whose body is the Ṛgveda! / Homage to you, the self of the gods; homage to you who are the Sāmaveda!
Homage to you, the syllable [Oṃ], whose nature is the Yajurveda, / to the one whose nature is the Ṛg-verses, and to the one who consists of the four Vedas!
Homage to you, the Veda and the Vedāṅgas, to you who possess all auxiliary parts! / Homage to you, Govinda, and to the one without beginning or end!
Homage to you who know the Veda, whose sole nature is preeminent, / the lord of Śrī, Bhū, and Līlā, the father of the universe; homage, homage!
Rudra said: / Having praised the god in the form of a boar with these and other hymns of praise, / they worshiped Hari, the lord of the self, with fragrances, flowers, and other offerings.
Being worshiped by those gods, the god gave them the boon they desired. / Sung in praise with joy by Gandharvas and Apsarases,
praised by the great sages, Hari vanished right there. / Having praised with these [words] in devotion, a devoted man, rising in the morning,

obtains the desired land, endowed with grain and fruit for a long time. / All this glory of Hari's boar incarnation has been told to you. / Now I shall tell of the man-lion incarnation; hear, O goddess with a beautiful face!
